open_points.subject: Expense-document binary read when the stored object is missing
open_points.text: R0-12 says "a refused document read answers that way also when its stored content is missing", making it indistinguishable from an unknown, cross-project or hidden read; A14 says "A missing source object is an explicit unavailable/not-found failure".
open_points.question: For an otherwise authorized, client-visible expense document whose source object is absent, is the response the concealed unknown/hidden response or an explicit storage-unavailable/not-found response?
options: Return the same concealed response used for unknown, cross-project and hidden documents.
Return an explicit unavailable/not-found storage failure.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the changed R0-12 rule and return the concealed response.

witness.initial: A visible ExpenseDocument exists for project P, the caller is authorized for P, and its file_ref points to an object that has disappeared from storage.
events: The caller requests the document binary by document_id.
The expense module authorizes the caller and passes the reference to binary storage.
Binary storage reports that the source object is missing.
outcomes: R0-12: the caller receives the same response as for an unknown, cross-project or hidden document.
A14: the caller receives an explicit unavailable/not-found failure.
witness.observer: The requesting caller can distinguish the HTTP/error response.

open_points.subject: Progress-photo binary read when the stored object is missing
open_points.text: R0-12 requires "a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered" to fail as "an explicit storage-unavailable error"; A14 says a missing source object is "an explicit unavailable/not-found failure".
open_points.question: When an authorized visible photo's source object is missing, must the failure be storage-unavailable, or may it be not-found?
options: Always return the explicit storage-unavailable error required by R0-12.
Return an explicit not-found error for a missing source object under A14.
Allow the storage adapter to choose between unavailable and not-found.
open_points.default_guess: Use the explicit storage-unavailable error required by the changed R0-12 text.

witness.initial: A client-visible ProgressPhoto exists for project P, the caller is authorized for P, and its file_ref points to an absent object.
events: The caller requests the photo binary by photo_id.
Binary storage reports that the object is missing.
outcomes: R0-12: the response is the explicit storage-unavailable error.
A14: the response may be an explicit not-found failure.
witness.observer: The requesting caller sees a different error classification or HTTP response.

open_points.subject: Expense-document storage failures other than missing, oversize or unlisted content
open_points.text: The changed rule conceals a document read "when its stored content is missing, oversize or unlisted" but does not say what happens for another failure to deliver stored document content; its photo rule instead covers every case where content "cannot be delivered".
open_points.question: How must an authorized document read fail for storage I/O errors not classified as missing, oversize or unlisted, such as permission denial, corrupt file_ref resolution, or an interrupted read?
options: Conceal every document delivery failure as the unknown/cross-project/hidden response.
Return an explicit storage-unavailable error, as for an undeliverable photo.
Use a distinct internal/storage error according to the underlying failure.
open_points.default_guess: Return an explicit storage-unavailable error for operational storage failures, while concealing only the three document conditions explicitly named.

witness.initial: A visible ExpenseDocument exists, its caller is authorized, its content would have an allowed size and type, but the storage backend cannot read it because access to the underlying file is denied.
events: The caller requests the document binary.
Storage resolution raises a permission or I/O failure before bytes are returned.
outcomes: One implementation treats every inability to deliver the document as the same concealed refusal used for missing content.
Another returns an explicit storage-unavailable or internal storage error because the concealment list names only missing, oversize and unlisted content.
witness.observer: The requesting caller sees a different response and can classify the failure differently.
